about: Pillar's enterprise-wide budgeting software was one of the first to use Graphical User Interfaces (GUIs) and object-oriented technology and to run over a network, allowing multiple simultaneous users. It was purchased by IMRS (NASDAQ:IMRS, now Hyperion, NASDAQ:HYSL) in 1994.

name: Pirus Networks
about: Pirus Networks developed storage and networking products. BVP seeded the company in late 1999; it was acquired in mid-2002 by Sun Microsystems.

name: Polaris Petroleum
about: BVP's Bill Burgin invested in the 1979 seed round of Polaris Petroleums, a Canadian company that explored and developed oil and gas properties in western Canada. Thirteen years later, in 1992, the company merged with Cabre Exploration (TSE:CBE).

name: Portrait Software
about: Portrait Software (LSE-AIM: PST) specializes in Customer Interaction Management solutions - software that helps build more responsive, more profitable customer relationships.

name: Postini
about: Provider of email security and management for the enterprise.

name: Powertel PCS Partners
about: Powertel operated a digital PCS wireless network in the Southeast. Bill Burgin led BVP's 1995 investment in the company. In 1996, Powertel PCS merged with its parent, InterCel, but kept the Powertel name. Deutsche Telecom (NYSE:DT) purchased the combined operations in 2001.
name_as_listed: Powertel PCS Partners (acq. by Deutsche Telecom)

name: PRE Solutions
about: A startup financial services company providing debit cards to the unbanked, teen, and immigrant markets.
name_as_listed: PRE Solutions (fka ITC Financial Services) (acq. by Incomm)

name: PSINet
about: PSINet was the first venture-backed Internet Service Provider in the world. BVP's David Cowan and Felda Hardymon invested in its early rounds starting in 1993. PSINet went public in May 1995 as NASDAQ:PSIX.

name: Pure Networks
about: The leading provider of home networking software and services.

name: Quadriserv
about: A start-up serving the market data needs of the securities lending industry.

name: Quantor
about: In 1974, BVP invested in this manufacturer of microfiche systems, which was acquired by NCR (NYSE:NCR) in 1978.

name: Quantum Effect Devices
about: QED manufactures high-performance MIPS-based micro-processors for applications in the communications industry. Rob Chandra led BVP's investment in the company's later rounds. In 2000, QED went public as NASDQ:QEDI and was acquired by PMC-Sierra (NASDAQ: PMCS)that same year.

name: Radiation Dynamics
about: In 1974, BVP invested in Radiation Dynamics, a developer of electron accelerators and radiation processing technology. Monsanto (NYSE:MON) acquired the company in 1979.

name: Register.com
about: Register.com provides domain name registration and related Internet services. BVP's David Cowan invested in the company in 1999; it went public as NASDAQ: RCOM the following year.

name: Resonext
about: Resonext Communications develops high frequency communications chips on CMOS technology.

name: Restore Medical
about: Restore Medical is developing a series of therapeutic devices to treat snoring and other sleep-disordered breathing conditions.

name: Retail Solutions
about: The leading RFID analytics and applications company.

name: Revver
about: Revver supports video creators by distributing their work and allowing them to earn money through attached advertisements.

name: Rico Auto Industries
about: Rico (BSE:RICOAUTO) designs and manufactures auto components for such firms as Ford, GM, and Cummins. The company is based in India.

name: Sahara Networks
about: Sahara, the first venture of Jon Reeves (who later founded Sirocco), developed ATM-based broadband access concentrators. BVP's Felda Hardymon invested in the company's first round. In 1997, Sahara was bought by BVP-backed Cascade Communications (NASDAQ: CSCC), a few months later by Ascend (NASDAQ:ASND), and finally by Lucent (NYSE:LU).
name_as_listed: Sahara Networks (acq. by Cascade, Ascend, and Lucent)

name: Sandbridge Technologies
about: Sandbridge Technologies develops semiconductors and compilers for broadband DSP (Digital Signal Processor) applications.

name: Sarovar Hotels & Resorts
about: One of the leading players in the hospitality industry in India, Sarovar manages a diverse portfolio that includes hotels, resorts, restaurants, and corporate hospitality.

name: Sarvega
about: Sarvega builds intelligent XML switches that enable Fortune 500 Enterprises to route information based on its meaning and value.

name: SciQuest.com
about: SciQuest develops software and services that streamline lab supply purchases and lab operations management. BVP invested in 1998 and the following year, SciQuest went public as NASDAQ:SQST.

name: Shriram EPC
about: A specialized engineering services company addressing the Indian infrastructure sector.

name: Siano Mobile Silicon
about: Making the chips for mobile digital TV.

name: Silicon Valley Solar
about: Silicon Valley Solar is a manufacturer of super high-efficiency flat-plate internal concentrator solar modules.

name: Sirocco Systems
about: Sirocco Systems was Jon Reeve's second venture and one of the pioneering developers of metropolitan area optical networking equipment. BVP's Felda Hardymon led the seed and A round investments in the company, which was subsequently purchased by Sycamore Networks (NASDAQ: SCMR) in 2000.

name: Sirtris Pharmaceuticals
about: A biopharmaceutical firm developing enzymes that activate our natural devences against disease.

name: SiteAdvisor, Inc.
about: Developing a centralized service that protects consumers from web-based security threats.

name: Skype
about: Skype is developing global peer-to-peer voice-over-Internet software and services.

name: Smart Machines
about: n 1997 BVP led an investment round in Smart Machines, a developer of robotic equipment for manufacturing semiconductors. Two years later, Brooks Automation (NASDAQ:BRKS) acquired the company.

name: Soleil Securities
about: Soleil is a newly formed NASD broker dealer that is dedicated to providing high-quality, ideologically independent research to institutional clients.

name: Sonus Networks
about: Sonus Networks, Inc. developed carrier-class voice infrastructure products for the public network. BVP's Felda Hardymon invested in the company in 1997. Sonus went public as NASDAQ:SONS in 2000.

name: Sparter
about: Creating an online marketplace for virtual items.

name: Staples
about: Staples invented the office superstore concept and today is the largest operator of office superstores in the world. BVP's Felda Hardymon and Bill Burgin invested in each of the company's four rounds, starting in 1986. It went public in 1989 as NASDAQ: SPLS.

name: Stream Machine
about: Stream Machine's technology provided the highest quality video for multiple home entertainment applications. Three years after BVP's first investment in 1998, the company was acquired by Cirrus Logic (NASDAQ:CRUS).
name_as_listed: Stream Machine Company (acq. by Cirrus Logic)

name: StreamBase
about: StreamBase Systems is delivering the world's first Stream Processing Engine for real-time data processing. Based on StreamSQL, StreamBase can process, analyze and respond to extremely high volumes of real-time data within milliseconds of arrival.

name: Sulconam
about: In 1957, BVP invested in Sulconam, a developer of technology to reclaim sulphur from refining operations. Forty years later, in 1997, BVP structured an exit. At the time, the company's annual dividend exceeded its cost basis.

name: Summit Microelectronics
about: Designs and sells programmable analog semiconductors.

name: Synergy Computer Graphics
about: BVP seeded Synergy, a manufacturer of high-performance color printers and plotters, in 1984. Four years later, Nippon Steel bought the operation.
name_as_listed: Synergy Computer Graphics (acq. by Nippon Steel)

name: Syntrex
about: Founded in 1979, Syntrex developed fault-tolerant information systems for the legal sector. After BVP participated in its three financing rounds, Syntrex went public in 1982 as NASDAQ:STRX.

name: System Management Arts
about: System Management Arts (SMARTS) develops network management and service assurance software for enterprise and service provider networks. It was acquired by EMC Corporation (NYSE:EMC).

name: SystemSoft
about: BVP's Felda Hardymon invested in the early rounds of SystemSoft, a developer of system-level software that managed computer utilities including power, connectivity, data, and disk organization. The company went public in 1994 as NASDAQ:SYSF.

name: Taqua
about: Taqua developed and marketed "Open Compact Exchange," a platform that allowed telecommunications carriers to offer enhanced services. The company was acquired by Tekelc (NASDAQ:TKLC)in 2004.

name: Telenet
about: Telenet was one of the first providers of public packet switching data communications. BVP invested in all three of its rounds, starting in 1975. GTE (NASDAQ:GTE) acquired the company in 1978.

name: Telica
about: Telica provides broadband switching systems. It was acquired by Lucent in 2004.

name: Telocity
about: Telocity was an early provider of residential broadband internet service provider. BVP's David Cowan co-led the first venture round in 1998. Telocity went public as NASDAQ: TLCT on March 31, 2001 (the last IPO of the dotcom era). Hughes' Electronics (NYSE: GMH) acquired the company later that year.

name: TeraBeam
about: TeraBeam provides businesses with fiberless optical connectivity to the Internet or corporate Intranets. It was acquired by YDI (OTCBB:YDIW) in 2004.

name: The Sports Authority
about: The Sports Authority pioneered the concept of a superstore for sporting goods and has become the largest full-line sporting goods retailer in the United States. Felda Hardymon and Bill Burgin participated in its 1987 and 1988 financing rounds. The Sports Authority went public in 1994 as NYSE: TSA.

name: Thinq Learning Solutions
about: THINQ is a one-stop source for corporate learning solutions.

name: Thomas Weisel Partners Group
about: An investment bank focusing on the technology markets.

name: Traffic.com
about: Traffic.com is creating America's premier traffic information franchise.

name: TransVascular
about: Develops innovative therapeutic alternative devices to allow surgeons to access tissues throughout the body less invasively.

name: TravCorps
about: TravCorps provided health care professionals for temporary and permanent assignments. BVP invested in its first institutional round in 1995; four years later the company merged with Cross Country Staffing and became Cross Country TravCorps. In 2001, the merged entity went public as NASDAQ: CCRN.

name: Trenwick
about: In 1979, BVP invested in the first round of this provider of reinsurance to Bermuda-based insurers. The company went public in 1986 as NASDAQ:TREN.

name: Trigo
about: Trigo creates enterprise software solutions for Product Information Management. In 2004, IBM (NYSE:IBM) acquired the company.

name: Tripwire
about: Tripwire is a software development company specializing in system security and policy compliance applications.

name: Tumbleweed
about: Tumbleweed's Integrated Messaging System extends existing e-mail and web applications by creating a secure, traceable and personalized online communication environment. BVP's David Cowan participated in the company's 1997 recapitalization. It went public in 1999 as (NASDAQ: TMWD), and has since acquired two other public BVP portfolio companies, Worldtalk (NASDAQ:WTLK) and Valicert (NASDAQ:VLCT).

name: U.S. Behavioral Health
about: In 1987, BVP's Chris Gabrieli invested in the first institutional round of U.S. Behavioral Health, a provider of outsourced mental health benefits for employer-sponsored health plans. BVP participated in two more rounds and served on the board until 1990, when the company was acquired by The Travelers Group (NYSE:TRV).
name_as_listed: U.S. Behavioral Health (acq. by The Travelers Group)

name: Ungermann-Bass
about: Ungermann-Bass pioneered local area networking (the term "LAN" was actually coined in the living room of BVP's Neill Brownstein). Brownstein led the first institutional investment in the company in 1980. Ungermann-Bass went public in 1983 as NASDAQ:UNGR.

name: Unipalm
about: Unipalm was the largest independent U.K. Internet Service Provider. Felda Hardymon led BVP's 1994 investment in Unipalm and it went public on the LSE in the same year. In 1995, it was acquired by UUnet Technologies (NASDAQ:UUNT). In 1996, the company underwent a partial MBO, and then was acquired by MFS Communications (NASDAQ:MFST) and a month later by WorldCom, Inc. (NASDAQ: WCOM).

name: ValiCert
about: Valicert provides security products for the Internet. After going public in 2000, it was purchased by Tumbleweed (NASDAQ:TMWD) three years later.

name: Verio
about: In 1996, BVP participated in an expansion round of Verio, a global ISP. Two years later, Verio went public as NASDAQ:VRIO, and was acquired by NTT (NYSE: NTT) in 2000.
name_as_listed: Verio (fka World-Net Access, acq. by NTT)

name: VeriSign
about: Verisign is the leading provider of trusted infrastructure services to website owners, enterprises, service providers and individuals. BVP's David Cowan co-founded Verisign in January 1995 as a spin-out from RSA, and served as the company's initial Chairman and CFO. The company went public in 1998 as NASDAQ:VRSN.

name: Veritas
about: Veritas developed storage management and software quality tools for use in open systems. In 1991, BVP's Neill Brownstein invested in the company, which went public in 1993 as (NASDAQ: VRTS).

name: Versant Object Technology
about: In 1990 BVP led an investment round to fund Versant, a pioneer of object-oriented databases. Versant went public as NASDAQ:VSNT in 1998.

name: Vertica Systems
about: Developing a revolutionary database system that will dramatically improve query performance for data warehouse applications.

name: VideoServer
about: VideoServer, seeded by BVP's Felda Hardymon, developed the first successful wide-area communications switch for video-conferencing among different platforms and encoding methods. VideoServer went public in 1995 as NASDAQ:VSVR, and in 1999 changed its name to Ezenia! (NASDAQ: EZEN).

name: Vimo
about: An online service providing decision support tools for business and individual users of consumer-driven healthcare.

name: VistaCare
about: BVP's Chris Gabrieli led the first round in VistaCare, now a leading hospice care provider that went public in 2002 as NASDAQ:VSTA.

name: Vitelic
about: Vitelic was an innovator in semiconductor technology, designing and manufacturing memory chips and logic products, such as DRAMs, SRAMs, EPROMS, and Flash memories. BVP participated in all four of its rounds, starting in 1984. The company was acquired by MOS Electronics Taiwan (Mosel) in 1991.

name: VMX
about: VMX invented automated voicemail systems. BVP invested in its first institutional round in 1978 and continued supporting the company until it went public in 1983 as NASDAQ: VMXI.

name: Voyant Technologies
about: A provider of teleconferencing services, Voyant acquired BVP's portfolio company Octave Communications in 2002. The following year, it merged with Polycom.

name: WaveSmith Networks
about: WaveSmith developed optical networking equipment for converging voice and data networks. BVP invested in every round. In 2003, Ciena (NASDAQ:CIEN) acquired the company.

name: Way Systems
about: Providing wireless point of sale service through a standard mobile phone platform.

name: WebSpective
about: In 1997 BVP led the first venture round of Webspective, a pioneer in load balancing software for networks. Inktomi (NASDAQ:INKT) acquired the company in 1999.

name: Wikia
about: An advertising-supported platform for developing and hosting community-based wikis.

name: Wize
about: Helping consumers decide what to buy by creating the Wize Rank based on reviews by consumers and experts compiled from all over the web.

name: WorkMetro
about: One of the nation�s premier locally-focused online recruiting solutions.

name: Worldtalk
about: BVP's David Cowan led several rounds in Worldtalk, starting in 1993. Worldtalk started out selling an email and directory switch. After going public in 1996 as NASDAQ:WTLK, Worldtalk focused on email security. In January 2000, the company was acquired by another BVP company, Tumbleweed (NASDAQ:TMWD).

name: Yelp
about: Internet service to help consumers find what's great -- and not so great -- in their neighborhood and beyond.

name: Zensys
about: The provider of wireless networking technology for control and status reading applications and the developer of Z-Wave, a low-cost, two-way, wireless mesh network communications technology.

name: Zopa
about: An online community linking lenders and borrowers.
